headline: Screening adoption and volume scaling across all vectors as tests become default behavior.

deltas.reads: Cologuard and new multi-cancer tests maintain steady expansion as the flagship screening franchise scales.
Blood-based colorectal cancer screening adoption accelerating rapidly, validating the friction-reduction thesis.
Screening revenue growing faster than test volume suggests improving reimbursement and ASP as coverage expands.
Oncology monitoring adoption doubling annually; Signatera and other cancer surveillance tests becoming routine.

deltas.change: double-digit organic growth in Advanced Diagnostics
deltas.reads: Direct-to-consumer screening behavior normalizing; consumers buying diagnostic tests independently.
Installed diagnostic systems and testing infrastructure compounding as installed base deepens.

momentum_note: The screening revolution is unmistakably accelerating. Exact Sciences holds steady but now sits inside a larger ecosystem where Guardant's Shield blood-based screening is growing 50% quarter-over-quarter and Natera's oncology tests are doubling annually. Quest is pulling screening into consumer awareness through questhealth.com, while Abbott's diagnostics segment accelerates at 12% YoY. The trend is not linear volume growth—it is participation becoming behavioral default. When Guardant's test volume jumps 50% in one quarter and reimbursement rates expand simultaneously, that signals the adoption curve is compressing. This is the moment when screening stops being a deliberate medical act and becomes infrastructure.
